subtitle: Differences between capital and financial cases
author: Moses Maimonides
intro: Rambam's Commentary on the Mishnah in the original 12th-century Judeo-Arabic. Hover a phrase to see its English light up; tap any word for a dictionary gloss.

aligned.ja: לא יקבל מנה מא יסתט'הר בה בעד ד'לך לאנא נקול באטנה פי הד'א אלט'היר או האולא אלשהוד אד' וקד קאל קבל אן לא ט'היר לה בוג'ה.
aligned.en: He will not accept any [later evidence] that he might invoke afterward to support his claim, for we say [in such a case] that there is some collusion in this supporting evidence or in these witnesses, since he had [already] stated that he had no supporting evidence whatsoever.

pairs.ja: לא יקבל מנה מא יסתט'הר בה
pairs.en: He will not accept any [later evidence] that he might invoke
collusion
supporting evidence
these witnesses

aligned.ja: אמא מתי קאל לי שהוד פי מדינת הים, או לי שטר הנאך, לא יסמע מנה, בל ימצ'י אלחכם בחסב אלחאצ'ר.
aligned.en: But if he said, "I have witnesses in such-and-such a city," or, "I have a document there," he is not heard, and rather the verdict proceeds according to what is presently available.

pairs.en: I have witnesses in such-and-such a city
I have a document there
he is not heard
the verdict proceeds according to what is presently available

aligned.ja: פאד'א ג'אב שהודה או ות'יקתה סותר את הדין ויחכם לה במא ט'הר לה, אד' ולם יקל פי אוליהֵ אלחאל אין לי עדים ואין לי ראיה.
aligned.en:
Then, [if afterward] he produces his witnesses or his document, he overturns the judgment, and a ruling is given for him in accordance with what has [now] become apparent to him—since at the outset of the matter he did not say, "I have no witnesses and no proof."

*Chapter Four.*

pairs.en: he produces his witnesses or his document
he overturns the judgment
in accordance with what has [now] become apparent to him
at the outset of the matter

pairs.ja: אין לי עדים ואין לי ראיה

aligned.ja: משנה [א]
aligned.en: Mishnah 1

aligned.ja: קולה אחד דיני ממונות בדרישה וחקירה, אנמא הו דבר תורה, ולכן כדי שלא תנעול דלת בפני לווין קאלוא אן לא יתקצי אלדרישה ואלחקירה בדיני ממונות.
aligned.en: His statement that "both monetary cases and [capital cases require] inquiry and examination" is [a requirement] by Torah law; but in order that "the door not be locked before borrowers," they ruled that inquiry and examination need not be carried to completion in monetary cases.

pairs.en: inquiry and examination
by Torah law
the door not be locked before borrowers
inquiry and examination need not be carried to completion
monetary cases

aligned.ja: ואמא בדיקה פלא יעתמד עליהא פי דיני ממונות ג'מלה ואחדה, אללהם אלא אן כאן פי ד'לך אלחכם באטנה כמא יקולון דין מרומה.
aligned.en: As for probing [interrogation], no reliance is placed upon it at all in monetary cases—except where there is collusion in that very judgment, as in what they call "a suspect case" (*din meruammeh*).

pairs.en: probing [interrogation]
no reliance is placed upon it
collusion
a suspect case

aligned.ja: ואלפרק בין אלדרישה ואלחקירה ואלבדיקה, אן אלחקירה ואלדרישה הי אלאשיא אלתי תפיד מעני פי אלחכם מת'ל קולנא כם אסלפה, ומתי אסלפה, ועלי אי וג'ה אסלפה, ופי אי מוצ'ע אסלפה אעני פי אי בלד.
aligned.en: The difference between inquiry and examination [on the one hand] and probing [on the other] is that examination and inquiry concern those matters that bear upon the substance of the verdict, such as our asking: How much did he lend him? When did he lend it to him? In what manner did he lend it? And in what place did he lend it—that is, in which town?

pairs.en: The difference between inquiry and examination [on the one hand] and probing [on the other]
bear upon the substance of the verdict
How much did he lend him
When did he lend it to him
in what place did he lend it

aligned.ja: ובדיקה הי אלתקצי פי אמור לא תפיד מעני מת'ל קולנא אי ת'וב כאן לבאס אלד'י אסלף או אלד'י תסלף חין אכ'ד' אלמאל, וג'אלסא כאן אחדהמא או ואקפא, ופי ת'וב חריר כאן אלמאל או פי ת'וב צוף, ומא נחי נחו הד'ה אלאשיא אלתי הי תקצי לא יפיד גרץ' פי אלחכם.
aligned.en: Probing [interrogation], by contrast, is the pursuit of matters that bear no substance [upon the verdict], such as our asking: What garment was the lender, or the borrower, wearing when he took the money? Was either of them seated or standing? Was the money in a silk garment or in a wool garment?—and whatever follows this pattern of inquiries that, being [merely] probing, yield nothing of relevance to the verdict.

pairs.en: the pursuit of matters that bear no substance [upon the verdict]

pairs.ja: אי ת'וב כאן לבאס אלד'י אסלף
pairs.en: What garment was the lender, or the borrower, wearing

aligned.ja: ועל פי שנים לחובה, מת'ל אן יקול אחד עשר דיין זכאי ות'לאת'הֵ עשר דיין חייב, אלד'י זאד עדד אלמחייבין על המזכין שנים וחיניד' יהרג.
aligned.en: "And by [the mouth of] two for liability"—as when eleven judges say "acquitted" and thirteen judges say "liable," in which case the number of those declaring liability exceeds those declaring acquittal by two, and only then is he put to death.

pairs.en: by [the mouth of] two for liability
eleven judges say "acquitted"

pairs.ja: זאד עדד אלמחייבין על המזכין שנים
pairs.en: the number of those declaring liability exceeds those declaring acquittal by two
is he put to death

aligned.ja: ואן קלת כיף ימכן ד'לך ובית דין אנמא הם כ"ג פקט כמא תקדם ולא ימכן אן יזיד אלמחייבין על המזכין שנים אלא אד'א כאן אלבית דין כ"ד, פג'ואב ד'לך הו אן יקול אחד עשר זכאי ואחד עשר חייב ואחד איני יודע אלד'י ילזם אן יוסיפו הדיינין שנים כמא תקדם, פיציר אלמתנאט'רין כ"ד וימכן פיהם מא ד'כרנא מן זיאדהֵ אלמחייבין עלי המזכין שנים.
aligned.en: Should you ask: How is this possible, when the court consists of only twenty-three, as stated above, so that the convicting judges cannot exceed the acquitting judges by two unless the court were twenty-four?—the answer is this: [the case arises] when eleven say "acquitted," eleven say "liable," and one says "I do not know," for then the judges must be increased by two, as stated above, so that the deliberating [judges] become twenty-four, and among them the increase we mentioned—of the convicting over the acquitting by two—becomes possible.

pairs.en: the court consists of only twenty-three
the judges must be increased by two
the deliberating [judges] become twenty-four

aligned.ja: ותעלק להד'א אלמעני מן קולה תעלי לא תהיה אחרי רבים לרעות, יעני אן אד'א כאן אלאכת'ר לרעה פלא תסמע מנהם אלא אן תכון כת'רה זאידה, והו אן יזיד אלד'י יחכמון לרעות את'נין פמא זאד.
aligned.en: To this matter attaches the verse, "Do not follow a multitude to do evil" (Exodus 23:2)—meaning that when the majority [inclines] toward harm, you do not heed them unless there is an additional surplus, namely that those who rule for harm exceed [the others] by two or more.

pairs.en: Do not follow a multitude to do evil
the majority [inclines] toward harm
an additional surplus

pairs.ja: יזיד אלד'י יחכמון לרעות את'נין פמא זאד
pairs.en: those who rule for harm exceed [the others] by two or more

aligned.ja: לפיכך אין דנין בערב שבת, לאן גמר דין יג'י פי אלסבת ולא ימכן אלקתל פי אלסבת לקולה לא תבערו אש בכל משבתיכם יריד בה ולו פי מושב בית דין לא יחרק פיה מן אסתחק אלחרק, וכד'לך באקי אלחדוד לא תקאם פי אלסבת.
aligned.en: "Therefore they do not judge on the eve of the Sabbath"—because the final verdict would fall on the Sabbath, and execution is not possible on the Sabbath, on account of the verse, "You shall kindle no fire throughout your dwellings on the Sabbath day" (Exodus 35:3), which intends [to forbid] even [that] in the session of the court the one liable to burning be burned; and likewise the other [forms of] punishment are not carried out on the Sabbath.

pairs.en: they do not judge on the eve of the Sabbath
the final verdict would fall on the Sabbath
You shall kindle no fire throughout your dwellings on the Sabbath day
the session of the court

pairs.ja: באקי אלחדוד לא תקאם פי אלסבת
pairs.en: the other [forms of] punishment are not carried out on the Sabbath

aligned.ja: משנה [ב]
aligned.en: Mishnah 2

aligned.ja: פי דיני נפשות לא יסמע כלאם אכברהם אלא אכ'ר אלקום, לאן אן תכלם אכברהם פי אלאול לא ימכן אלבקיה אלכ'לאף עליה לקולה לא תענה על ריב.
aligned.en: In capital cases the opinion of the greatest among them is not heard until [the opinions of] the rest of the company [have been heard], for if the greatest among them were to speak first, it would not be possible for the rest to differ with him, on account of the verse, "You shall not respond in a dispute [to incline]" (Exodus 23:2)—where it is written *rav*

pairs.en: capital cases

pairs.ja: לא יסמע כלאם אכברהם אלא אכ'ר אלקום
pairs.en: the opinion of the greatest among them is not heard until [the opinions of] the rest of the company [have been heard]
it would not be possible for the rest to differ with him
You shall not respond in a dispute

aligned.ja: והו מכתוב רב, אי מא תכלם פיה עט'ים פי אלעלם לא תכ'אלף עליה, פלד'לך יוכ'ר סמאע ראיה.
aligned.en: : that is, one whose word is weighty in learning, you may not contradict. For this reason the hearing of his opinion is deferred.

pairs.en: weighty in learning
you may not contradict
the hearing of his opinion is deferred

aligned.ja: וקולה הכל כשרים לדון, ולו גר אד'א כאנת אמה מן ישראל. וכד'לך ממזר כשר לדון דיני ממונות.
aligned.en: As for his statement, "All are fit to judge"—this includes even a convert, (JA: *גר* (*ger*). A convert may judge provided his mother is a born Israelite.) provided his mother is of Israel. Likewise a *mamzer* is fit to judge monetary cases.

pairs.en: All are fit to judge
a convert
his mother is of Israel
a *mamzer* is fit to judge monetary cases

aligned.ja: משנה [ג]
aligned.en: Mishnah 3

aligned.ja: עגולה, דאירה.

aligned.ja: ועלהֵ קול ר' יהודה ליכון שאהדין עלי אלמזכין ושאהדין עלי אלמחיבין. והלכה כחכמים.
aligned.en: And to this attaches R. Yehuda's view that there should be witnesses [recorded] for those who acquit and witnesses for those who convict. But the law is in accordance with the Sages.

aligned.ja: משנה [ד]
aligned.en: Mishnah 4

aligned.ja: קד תבין מן קולנא פי אלפרק אלאול מן הד'ה אלמסכתא אן כל בית דין של עשרים ושלשה בין ידיהם שלש שורות, ופי כל שורה עשרים ושלשה איצ'א מרתבין אול ות'אני ות'אלת' אלי אכ'רהם עלי מרתבתהם פי אלעלם.
aligned.en: It has already been made clear from what we said in the first chapter of this tractate that before every court of twenty-three there are three rows, and in each row there are likewise twenty-three [persons], arranged first, second, third, and so on to the last, according to their rank in learning.
